use: Site > City-wide policy maps > enable 5A or Primary Transit Network. Map source switches between City vector network and Published PDF comparison. Click a route or hub for designation and source. Opacity supports 0-100%.
snapshotRefresh: python tools/policy_maps/fetch_transport_vectors.py --output <review-directory>; review output before promoting both GeoJSON files to frontend/public/policy-maps/transport-vectors-v1. A changed schema or release should bump the snapshot directory and query key.
deployment: Both GeoJSON files are static public assets. No City API credentials or backend changes. When using CITYPROMPT_PUBLIC_DIR for local hydrated assets, copy these two files to that root as well and restart Vite to index new public paths.
dataHandling: EPSG:4326 coordinates rounded to six decimals; no PDF tracing, snapping or line simplification. Stable source IDs deduplicate overlapping City views. 5A segments with identical category, priority and source are grouped into MultiLineStrings without moving vertices.
rendering: Screen-space route lines batched by category, instanced hub symbols, cached on-demand snapshots. Geometry rebuilt only when snapshot, height or layer identity changes; not each animation frame.
browserVerified: 5A riverside pathway visually follows the pathway around the Bow Arts trial site in top view
Clicking a 5A route opens its designation, primary network priority, explanation and official City feature service
Clicking a regional transit hub opens its explanation and source
Transit opacity zero hides geometry and clears selection; 100 percent restores it
Switch between PDF and vector for both networks; toggle layers off/on
5A and transit vector closeups retain crisp symbols while PDF symbols become broad and pixelated
After correcting hub disposal, toggling transit on/off produced no new browser error logs during the final trial
limits: Vector datasets are not a one-to-one reproduction of the 2026 PDF. Transit has generic skeletal LRT classes rather than named Red/Blue/Green lines; regional rail corridors and urban structure background are absent.
5A contains route segments; the PDF also has crossing recommendations, transit, schools and recreation symbols.
5A includes primary and secondary proposed route classes as supplied by the City; priority appears in route details.
Policy geometry remains conceptual, not surveyed. Top View avoids 3D terrain parallax; the overlay uses the existing project terrain reference height, not per-vertex terrain sampling.
No representative student laptop or 40-user load test was performed. No measured FPS comparison is claimed.
Dash lengths are 30 m with 20 m gaps; proposed routes may resemble solid lines at city-wide overview scale. Their designation remains available by clicking.

verification.vitest: 40 passed across 10 policyPlans test files, including a failing-then-passing hub disposal regression

review: Independent read-only code review found no additional critical or important issues. Reported disposal failure fixed and verified. Minor: proposed-route world-distance dashes can become subpixel at city-wide zoom; neighbourhood/site comparisons are the verified pilot scale.
